name: Pierre Auger Observatory hybrid detector

placements.quote: Beginning of the construction of the observatory.
placements.note: Placement point is the Observatory campus; the physical array of stations is spread over the surrounding 3000 km^2 (see site:malargue-auger notes).

technology.value: Hybrid detector: a surface array of water-Cherenkov tanks sampling air-shower particles at ground level, cross-checked by fluorescence telescopes imaging ultraviolet light from the shower's longitudinal development.
technology.quote: one using water placed in surface detector tanks... another tracking the development of air showers by observing ultraviolet light emitted high in the Earth's atmosphere

intervals.label: construction
intervals.quote: Beginning of the construction of the observatory.

intervals.label: data taking (partial then full array)
intervals.quote: First physics results are reported from more than 100 surface detector stations.

intervals.label: AugerPrime upgrade
intervals.quote: scintillator and radio detectors have been installed atop each existing water-Cherenkov detector
intervals.note: Adds surface scintillator detectors (SSD), upgraded station electronics (UUB), radio antennas (RD) and underground muon counters (UMD) to each existing water-Cherenkov station; RD deployment reported complete November 2024, UMD partial as of the August 2025 status paper.

description.value: Array of 1660 water-Cherenkov detector tanks spread over 3000 km^2, sampling the particle density of extensive air showers at ground level.

27 optical telescopes in four buildings overlooking the surface array, imaging the ultraviolet fluorescence light emitted by nitrogen molecules excited along an air shower's path through the atmosphere.

summary.plain: A two-in-one detector: 1660 tanks of water spread over 3000 square kilometres sense particles from cosmic-ray showers reaching the ground, while 27 telescopes watch the same showers develop as faint ultraviolet flashes in the night sky.
summary.technical: Hybrid surface-detector/fluorescence-detector system: 1660 water-Cherenkov tanks on a 1.5 km grid across 3000 km^2, plus 27 fluorescence telescopes in four buildings; currently being upgraded (AugerPrime) with scintillator panels, radio antennas, upgraded electronics and underground muon counters on each surface station.
